function: DDPG learns incremental positions of the base station's and user's fluid antennas, alternating with convex beamforming, to maximize the communication rate under a sensing-gain constraint (p. 3).
system: p. 2, 4: ISAC base station with 4/8/12 fluid antennas, one user with one fluid antenna, 1 or 3 sensing targets, far-field multipath; no RIS; band not stated.
method: p. 3: DDPG actor-critic (three-layer actor, 400/300-neuron critic), reinforcement learning trained offline, inside a block coordinate descent with convex-optimization beamforming (CVX).
data_channel: p. 2-4: custom simulation: far-field multipath model with random angles in [0, pi], diagonal path response with LoS/NLoS power ratio 1, three paths; no standard or measured channel.
test_conditions: p. 4: simulated random angles; results per N, K, M and SNR 0-30 dB; paper does not describe separate training and test conditions.
baselines: p. 4: non-learned fixed-position antennas (FPA) and particle swarm optimization (PSO); no earlier learned method compared.
metrics: p. 4: average and maximum communication rate (bps/Hz) versus SNR; sensing gain used as a constraint.
complexity: p. 4: offline DDPG training O(Neps x Tsteps x L x W^2); online antenna positioning O(N) forward pass; beamforming SDP O(N^3.5) to O(N^6); no runtime.
q1_support: p. 4: "We assume that the number of transmit and receive paths as D = I = 3." The channel is a custom far-field multipath model with random angles and a diagonal path response; no 3GPP TR 38.901 or 38.811, DeepMIMO, or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 4: "the proposed DRL framework seamlessly adapts to multiuser setups" is a claim, not a test of a trained model in a new setting; results are given per N, K, M and SNR and no train-test split or adaptation is described.
q3_support: p. 4: "the superiority of the proposed approach is evident when comparing the ideal performance against the particle swarm optimization (PSO)"; the FPA baseline is also non-learned (Fig. 1(a)). No earlier learned method, such as the DRL work [13] cited in the introduction, is compared.
q4_support: p. 4: "antenna positioning via DRL requires only a fast O(N) forward pass"; the same paragraph gives the offline training order O(Neps x Tsteps x L x W^2) and the SDP order O(N^3.5) to O(N^6).
q5_support: p. 4: "using the newly generated simulation results" shows the data are the authors' own simulations; no code or data link, public dataset, or measured data is given.
notes: Research letter; title and DOI match on p. 1. Area 5: the DDPG positions the fluid antennas of the base station and the user while the transmit covariance is solved by CVX in a block coordinate descent, so the joint antenna-position and beamforming design with a sensing-gain constraint is read as ISAC beam design, not antenna hardware design; the reviewer may confirm this against the antenna-hardware-design exclusion. The system model has one user, but Fig. 1(b) varies the number of users M (1 and 3). q3 is 0 because only FPA and PSO are compared.
